searchText: I disagree that Frame Transactions (EIP-8141) is only about a theoretical intermediate step. It changes the rules so that accounts are in charge of validating their own transactions. This means we basically never have to change the tx signature again because it completely removes the concept of signatures from the core protocol. To make PQ signatures viable, the protocol will move to provide building blocks such as precompiles for relevant signature algorithms. However, you are also right in that the EOA transition still has to occur eventually. EIP-8141 does not fully solve quantum computer readiness because the existing ECDSA keys will keep working for the time being. Schemes for migrating EOAs off of ECDSA are still being designed. I have a catastrophic vulnerability that renders security obsolete this vulnerability that gives access to any wallet in (0/1) time is completely independent of ecc and does not rely on any aspect of cryptology to operate it's an isolated unrelated system that cripples encryption at its most basic fundamental level Share the private key for a chosen address (e.g., address 1), or a transaction signed by a chosen address. Without one of those, it is unlikely anyone will believe you. Use the bug bounty program. I'm trying to do this responsibly but it's so damn hard Every time I look for contact info on a site it sends me to discord Yes I have read all your messages. You are making extraordinary claims without the skillset to actually verify them. It should come as no surprise that people are highly sceptical. If you have a mathematical model/proof to justify your claim, submit it via the bug bounty. There is an email address listed in https://ethereum.org/bug-bounty/ for submissions. excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content:
I disagree that Frame Transactions (EIP-8141) is only about a theoretical intermediate step. It changes the rules so that accounts are in charge of validating their own transactions. This means we basically never have to change the tx signature again because it completely removes the concept of signatures from the core protocol. 

To make PQ signatures viable, the protocol will move to provide building blocks such as precompiles for relevant signature algorithms.

However, you are also right in that the EOA transition still has to occur eventually. EIP-8141 does not fully solve quantum computer readiness because the existing ECDSA keys will keep working for the time being. Schemes for migrating EOAs off of ECDSA are still being designed.
